It addresses the severe performance degradation and artifact generation (floaters) that standard hash-only encoders exhibit with sparse views [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Nerfacto, with its hash-encoding, degrades heavily when input views are sparse' and that the proposed method (HE + FE8) 'outperforms Nerfacto (hash-only) on sparse inputs, avoiding degradation and floaters.' This directly supports the claim that the method addresses the severe performance degradation and artifact generation (floaters) exhibited by standard hash-only encoders with sparse views.
supported
Unlike hash-only baselines, HE+FE augments hash lookups with frequency levels to stabilize reconstruction, while training significantly faster than frequency-only alternatives like MIP-NeRF 360 [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed method (HE + FE) outperforms Nerfacto (described as hash-encoding/hash-only in the context of degradation) and achieves results comparable to MIP-NeRF 360 (described as frequency-encoding/frequency-only). Furthermore, the text confirms that the proposed method trains in approximately 5 minutes, while MIP-NeRF 360 requires around 2 hours, supporting the claim of significantly faster training.
